## Household and background

Marisol Reyes (born June 14, 1989) divorced in 2023 and has lived with her two children at 87 Larkspur Lane since. Mateo (born April 8, 2013 — 12) and Lucia (born September 27, 2018 — 7) are her biological children; they lived with her for all twelve months of 2025 and neither provided any of their own support. She pays the entire cost of the apartment and everything in it.

She is a unit coordinator at Anytown Regional Medical Center — one W-2, box 1 wages $41,285.00, box 2 federal withholding $1,860.00. That is the household's only income: no interest (her account is a fee-free checking account), no investments, no side work.

## Interview

**Q.** Who lived in your home during 2025, and for how many months?

**A.** Just me and the two kids, all twelve months. Nobody else.

**Q.** Did anyone else — your ex-husband, a grandparent — support them or try to claim them?

**A.** No. He doesn't pay support and he doesn't file for them. I've never signed anything letting anyone else claim them.

**Q.** Did either child have a job or any income of their own?

**A.** No. Mateo does chores for pocket money, nothing reportable.

**Q.** Do you pay more than half the cost of keeping up the home?

**A.** I pay all of it — rent, utilities, groceries, everything.

**Q.** Do all three of you have Social Security numbers, and is there any restriction printed on the cards?

**A.** Yes, all three of us, and no restrictions — they're the normal cards.

**Q.** Has the IRS ever disallowed your child tax credit or earned income credit?

**A.** No, never — I've always just filed a plain return.

**Q.** Did you pay anyone for child care so you could work?

**A.** Not this year. My mother watches Lucia after school and Mateo lets himself in — so there's nothing to claim for care.
